name: copilot-provider
description: Sessions through GitHub Copilot CLI, and the stage prompts the default SDLC sends when it starts or resumes one.

stability.note: Run live in a scratch Grid workspace on 2026-09-04 against @github/copilot 1.0.83 (authenticated non-interactively through the gh CLI's own OAuth token — no device-code flow was needed on this machine). Spawn itself works: a card reached prepare with an active session, and copilot-home/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl was written at exactly the path the manifest declares, with real session.start/hook/message events in it. Two gaps surfaced, both on core's side rather than this manifest: (1) core's /api/session/messages and its live tail never pass permissions.spawn.transcript.map into transcript.readConversation, so this provider's transcript does not render as chat anywhere in Grid's UI even though the file on disk is correct and populated — transcript.js's mapEvent exists but nothing wires it to a real caller yet. (2) the isolation degrade (capabilities().isolation: 'none') does work — a second concurrent session was refused with 'waiting: Copilot (GitHub Copilot CLI) cannot isolate two accounts on one machine' — but only reaches the UI when the caller reports the failure synchronously (a user-initiated Start does); the automatic spawn fired when a card arrives at prepare swallows the identical refusal into a server console.error with nothing recorded on the card, so on that path — likely the common one — it is not visible on the card. Separately, hook installation failed under this test's directory layout ('Grid does not write into a repository to make one of its own features work'), so Grid could not see this run's status via hooks, and its last_status sat on 'waiting' rather than ever reaching 'idle' for the life of the run, consistent with the known idle-latch gap tracked elsewhere. Loading this manifest at all also needs core's pluginhost to accept the 'trust' spawn key (core commit 33ba7d4); a core build without that skips this plugin entirely with 'unknown spawn key "trust"'. Not exercised: the stage prompts' own correctness, and the resumed-session-writes-into-shared-checkout question — this run's scratch project had no folder wired to its thread, so no worktree was ever cut to test against.
